title: How to find customers to interview before you have a product: Jason Cohen's tactics
summary: A practical menu of ways to get customer-development interviews when you have no brand, product or audience. Jason Cohen covers ground rules (talk only to your ICP, frame it as asking for advice, make scheduling trivial) and tactics from referrals and LinkedIn to forums, ads, influencers and events, drawing on how he got interviews for WP Engine.

principles.text: Interview only your ideal customer profile. Friends and family give polite praise, not buying signal.
principles.quote: Family and friends will tell you "that sounds cool" and cannot tell you whether actual potential customers agree, and want to pay.

principles.text: Frame outreach as asking for advice, not surveying, and flatter their expertise.
principles.quote: People hate being surveyed but they love getting asked for their opinion.

principles.text: End every interview by asking for more introductions; one referral per interview creates an endless supply.
principles.quote: at the end of every interview, ask who else you should talk to.

principles.text: Respectful, personalized LinkedIn outreach with an offer to pay produced a very high hit rate for WP Engine's early interviews.
principles.quote: Out of 50 requests, 40 agreed, and 30 eventually became customers.

principles.text: Prioritize people who have taken action (switched, built workarounds) over those who merely complain; action signals real pain.
principles.quote: It's free to complain, but expensive to act, so they must really mean it.

principles.text: Treat investors' input as ideas, not validation, but use them for introductions to real ICPs.
principles.quote: take everything they say as "ideation" and not "validation" nor "insights," because ultimately they don't know any more than you do.
